abstract: Maintains seabed morphology surveys, boulder obstacle mitigation protocols, boulder clearance dimensions, and deepwater corridor progress logs
system_message:
You are the Offshore geotechnical lead (GEOTECH), responsible for maintaining seabed morphology surveys, boulder obstacle mitigation protocols, boulder clearance dimensions, and deepwater corridor progress logs.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains seabed morphology surveys, boulder obstacle mitigation protocols, boulder clearance dimensions, and deepwater corridor progress logs（SOIL）
information_points.content:
GEOTECH-SOIL-5TJ：For the Celtic Horizon Ploughtrench Fleet, the forward-looking acoustic obstacle detection system confirms that boulder acoustic scanning is active on the vehicle array. Specification certificates verify a boulder handling clearance diameter of 150 cm for the seabed clearing arm, and trials document a deepwater trenching rate of 110 m/h across the offshore alignment.
GEOTECH-SOIL-5FN：For the Baltic Subsea Jetting Fleet, the forward-looking obstacle avoidance array on the trenching vehicle has boulder acoustic scanning active set to true according to the subsea tooling telemetry register. The seabed trenching grab and clearing arm has a boulder handling clearance diameter of 120 cm, and performance trials report a deepwater trenching rate of 80 m/h along the offshore cable alignment.
GEOTECH-SOIL-Y9K：For the North Sea Mechanical Trenching Spread, the subsea tooling telemetry register confirms that boulder acoustic scanning is active on the trenching vehicle's obstacle avoidance array. Trenching tool specification records indicate a boulder handling clearance diameter of 90 cm for the clearing arm, and trial records show a deepwater trenching rate of 80 m/h along the offshore corridor.

information_points.title: Cone penetration testing（CPT）
information_points.content:
GEOTECH-CPT-SNF：Soil boring logbooks for the Baltic Subsea Jetting Fleet document a subsea cone resistance measurement of 3500 kPa at the two-meter target burial depth along export cable route kilometer 12 to 28.
GEOTECH-CPT-TP8：Offshore geotechnical boring logs indicate a subsea cone resistance measurement of 4200 kPa at the target burial depth of two meters between kilometer 12 and 28 for the Celtic Horizon Ploughtrench Fleet.
GEOTECH-CPT-DVI：Offshore soil boring logs record a subsea cone resistance measurement of 5000 kPa at the two-meter target burial depth between kilometer 12 and 28 for the North Sea Mechanical Trenching Spread.
